decision.reason: S25 PCSE holdout HOLDOUT-DTI 0.0450 (CI 0.0380-0.0525) is below the same-fold random-K control 0.0699 (CI 0.0667-0.0731); paired difference -0.0248 (CI -0.0324 to -0.0169), 0/4 folds.

irregularities_for_review: Holdout DTI values (about 0.05-0.07) are far below public leaderboard scores (0.2-0.45); the holdout is not calibrated to the leaderboard and must not be treated as a score estimate.

A random-K placement beats the PCSE operator on the holdout. This suggests the holdout rewards spatially spread predictions or that the operator anti-correlates with holdout truth; it has not been diagnosed.
Old GEMSDOE submissions were generated with the full catalogue visible, so evaluating them on the holdout is not a clean test of their fault-finding ability.
The user-quoted 0.4413 top score does not appear on the live public board observed here (top 0.4544).
GEMSDOE24-36 scores are user-supplied and unverified; no organizer receipt was available.
next_steps: Assign a method lane explicitly (the user's protocol paragraph is ambiguous about lane assignment).
Reset the experiment clock by an explicit user-authorized session record before any experiment.
Diagnose why random-K beats PCSE on the holdout before proposing any new operator.

Consider graded (non-binary) predictions: the official DTI accepts probabilities in [0,1], and the FP/FN weighting makes soft confidence a distinct lever from binary dots. Test on the holdout before any slot.
